ratings_why.fun: Three real routes with a clear tier ladder and a steep, satisfying late game; turns 2-4 feel thin because own-board duels only move stats.
ratings_why.distinct: Over a 7: one size-compare verb aimed at your board, the shop and the enemy, plus losing to a shop unit on purpose to buy it and empty slots scoring as survivors, is unlike any tribe today.

verdict_why: Two rules still can't be read exactly (Cantor's riders, the Duel minimum against a 1-Health loser); the rest should settle.

points.text: Say whether a card's rider repeats with the duel (Lek Marshal's +1/+2, Edge-Strutter's +3/+3, Squire Konrad's +1/+1), or only the take.
Duel says 'at least 1 of each' and 'never takes the last Health'. Say what the victor gets from a loser on 1 Health.
Golden Sir Brennbart drops duelled shop units to 1 gold, and they sell for 1, so with Pilgrim every buy is free. A floor of 2 keeps the idea if that proves loose.
The early curve is flat: Konrad and Marshal mostly shuffle stats. One early unit that brings in stats from the shop or enemy at Tier 1-2 would let the climb start sooner.

standouts.why: Lord of the Old Lek makes the lone champion a real win plan: doubling plus empty slots counting for damage.
Dame Reisig turns losing a shop duel into a deliberate buy, the tribe's most surprising decision.
Pilgrim from Sprucehold turns every refresh into champion growth; a capstone you build toward from Tier 2.

weakest.why: Grit Pit Elder is a plain +1/+1 counter with no decision attached.
Bristle-Beard Rival only works on smaller attackers and feeds bigger ones; a one-sided Tier 5.
Pennon-Bearer leans on the rounding floor and falls off after the first few turns.

flags.note: With Keeper of the Gizzard Stones and Cantor it takes three quarters of every shop unit three times a turn, far past the Tier 6 top. It grows with shop size, not itself, so it is not a loop.
Ottokar with Keeper and Cantor takes three quarters of every smaller enemy at Start of Combat and can then outgrow the big one; the only counterplay is a taller enemy.
Golden Brennbart makes duelled shop units cost the same as they sell for; free buys feed The Chronicler and triples.
Doubling an already huge champion every fight, plus six damage per win from empty slots, may end games fast.
Doesn't say whether the riders on a duel repeat.
